# Manual orchestration

Every model call re-sends the caller's whole context; in the 2026-10-05 to 10-09 baseline about 73% of estimated quota spend was that re-send. Most rules in this skill either remove a call or lower what each call carries.

Use model judgment to divide an authorized objective into coherent outcomes whose evidence and ownership can be checked. Keep the accepted objective, authority, source identity, unresolved work and review requirements visible. Packet precision is not proof that all obligations were found; test the proposed decomposition against the owning contract and relevant boundaries before dispatch and when new facts appear. The route, slice size and order may change when evidence warrants it.

## Load by role

There are two levels. The supervisor is the top-level role (the root), and the user is its parent. It dispatches builders directly and launches reviewers separately; no coordinator sits above it and no supervisor sits between it and its workers.

- When forming or revising an organization, including during ongoing implementation with no new dispatch, launch or discovery assignment: [organization formation](references/organization-formation.md) - reviewable candidates, branch discovery and revision authority.

- **Supervisor** (top level): [supervisor](references/supervisor.md) - scope and budget, decomposition, packets, dispatch, validation, review collection, integration.
- **Worker or reviewer**: [worker](references/worker.md) - one coherent bounded assignment.
- **Every role**: [call cost](references/call-cost.md) - waiting, batching, request sizing.
- **Supervisor**: [context boundary](references/context-boundary.md) - retained or fresh before dispatch, transfer, roots. Workers carry their own mid-task check.
- When considering same-session context replacement: [same-session continuity](references/same-session-context.md) - authority, durable meaning, supported controls, visible resumption and recovery.
- **On Codex**, with any role: [Codex host](references/codex-host.md) - builder children, separate top-level reviewers, service tier and identity binding.
- **On Claude Code** (Anthropic models), with any role: [anthropic host](references/anthropic-host.md) - tool mapping, transcript-based context check.
- When launching, continuing or collecting a **Pi** role: [Pi host](references/pi-host.md) - API or subscription lane, per-launch service tier, turn observation, no-network container mode.
- After a run: [measurement](references/measurement.md). For a concrete artifact example: [demonstrated forms](references/demonstrated-forms.md).

Repository instructions and owning contracts still govern each role.

## Launching a child

At launch, give the child its packet and tell it to load this skill for its role: invoke `$manual-orchestration`, or read `skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md` in the repository when the skill is not installed. It loads its own references; do not paste this skill or other guidance documents into its brief.

After launch, verify the role's actual session ID and rollout from recorded lineage, using the host reference's lookup for its launch mechanism, then send its identity binding: session ID, rollout, parent/collection owner, continuation path, and the pinned context-status binary path and SHA-256. An ID cannot be verified before the session exists, and a role name or inherited `CODEX_THREAD_ID` can name another session. The role acknowledges the binding at its next boundary and records it in its continuation. For a retained role, deliver the binding explicitly once and expect it in the continuation thereafter.

## Invariants

Separate worker completion, unfinished continuation, acceptance of a bounded subject, private readiness, and integration; the supervisor makes the last three, and they remain separate decisions. Carry exact source, subject, binary/schema and evidence identity where those affect the claim; preserve failures and uncertainty. Refresh the *meaning* of affected claims when source or assumptions change, not just their hashes. Record requested model/effort separately from observed identity, and leave unavailable measurements unknown. The supervisor retains responsibility for collecting required child results and owned processes.

This is a manual coordination adapter. In a configured Slice Builder campaign, use its owning [skill and receipt contract](../slice-builder/SKILL.md) unless that contract's owner accepts compatible continuation semantics. An unfinished manual `handoff_ready` is not its terminal `audit_receipt`, `handoff_receipt`, or gate success. The skill grants no new mutation, provider, review, acceptance or publication authority.

## Deterministic outer host

The optional [manual host](references/manual-host.md) composes native Codex dispatch, owned observations, exact-turn collection and acknowledged receipts for an explicitly authorized objective. It leaves semantic decisions and existing domain records with their owners.

## Scripts

- `scripts/provision_manual_host.sh [repo]` - build and pin the optional Rust manual host with its compatible adapter bundle; no global activation.
- `scripts/provision_context_status.sh [repo]` - build and pin the context-status binary outside the shared target; prints path and SHA-256.
- `scripts/child_context.py` - `check` one Codex session, `tree` a parent's children, or `claude` a Claude Code subagent transcript against the trigger and observed compaction band; writes a record to retain.
- `scripts/role_host.py` - host a role or child as a Claude `--bg`, Codex app-server or Pi session: `launch` (with `--parent` to record it in the ledger), `status`, `deliver`, `retire`, `children`, `whoami`. Pi launches name a lane with `--auth api|subscription` and may set `--service-tier` on the api lane; `--container` runs each turn without network behind a host egress proxy (`scripts/pi_container.py`); see [Pi host](references/pi-host.md). Codex also supports `rename`, `archive`, and `unarchive` without a model turn, plus `settings --rollout` to observe applied model/effort/tier for continuation. Detects and stops a Claude copy-on-resume fork.
- `scripts/auto_continue.py` - bounded foreground same-SID compaction and attributed recovery; use under [same-session continuity](references/same-session-context.md#foreground-automatic-continuation-on-the-codex-app-server).
- `scripts/root_rotation.py` - root transfer gate: `prepare` publishes continuation lineage and stops at `awaiting_authority`; `commit` or `watch` checks that the handoff is still available, launches the successor, waits for its typed `adopt` and retires or keeps the predecessor. `--title` provides a readable task name. See [context boundary](references/context-boundary.md#roots).
- `scripts/custody.py` - `run` a build or test, or a plan of them, recording PIDs, wait status, output and input digests and leftover processes; `freeze` a tree outside the repository into a manifest, archive and baseline diff. See [worker](references/worker.md#builds-tests-and-frozen-subjects).
- `scripts/scope_budget.py` - original scope, additions, the objective's sessions and its cost limits in the assignment record; `check` reports spend and time and says whether to reconsider or stop. See [supervisor](references/supervisor.md#scope-and-budget).
- `scripts/handoff_validator.py` - checks a root handoff's referents (paths, path-bound digests, labelled git refs, placeholders): 0 pass, 21 defect, 32 not established.

# Worker or reviewer: one coherent assignment

Own the packet's bounded engineering outcome, assigned files and launched processes. At entry, acknowledge the exact packet, authority and source/subject revisions. Your parent sends your identity binding after launch - verified session ID, rollout, parent/collection owner, continuation path, context-status binary and digest; acknowledge it at your next boundary and record it in your continuation. Verify current source and runtime inputs before relying on prior evidence. Read DESIGN.md as AGENTS.md requires; PHILOSOPHY.md in full only for design, planning or doctrine review. Read the coordination board at startup, after compaction and before claims or consequential operations, not as a loop. Before freezing a contract or route revision, check its premises against the packet's settled facts. Select the implementation and checks that establish the actual outcome. Report a discovered requirement gap, stale premise or ownership conflict to the supervisor before expanding scope or silently reclassifying the task. Do not start new child agents or next-slice work unless the packet assigns it.

Follow [call cost](call-cost.md): batch, size requests, do not poll, and message the parent only for a result, a decision, a blocker or a decision-relevant risk.

## Context

When assigned implementer discovery for an organization candidate, use [organization formation](organization-formation.md) to report bounded findings and whether you can own a coherent implementation outcome.

Read only what your packet's read list names; reading spends the same budget as writing. Prefer signatures (`grep -n 'pub fn'`) and targeted line ranges over whole files, batch independent reads, and commit after each independently passing unit.

Keep a compact continuation current as decisions and validation state change, not only when handing off: a compaction takes the window without asking, and the next context holds only what you wrote down. You do not decide the context for your *next* assignment; your parent checks that before dispatching it, because only the parent knows that task's size.

**Mid-task check.** At each logical boundary inside the assignment - before each substantial phase, not once - and again before writing your result if an earlier reading was above about 120,000, run (`<skill-dir>` is the manual-orchestration skill's directory):

```
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/child_context.py \
  --binary <pinned path> --sha256 <digest> check --session <your id> --rollout <your rollout>
```

The script compares your latest input with a trigger of 200,000 tokens and a band floor of 235,000. The floor sits just under the lowest automatic compaction observed: Astra from 239,130, and Sol 6.1 sessions under the 250,000 compaction limit at 248,987 ([measured basis](context-boundary.md#measured-basis)). Both levels are a hypothesis (H2), not a rule. If you are over it and the remaining work is substantial, prepare a handoff; otherwise continue. Record the reading, decision and reason in your continuation. Continuing past the trigger risks a compaction mid-task, after which the rest of the work is done from your continuation alone. If your parent bound a context listener to you, a current observation from it counts as the reading ([session control](context-control.md#what-to-do-with-an-observation)). Use only the binary you were given - do not build to check context, because a build lock can block observation for everyone. If usage cannot be read, record `usage_unavailable` with the script's class; never guess or treat it as zero. An `epoch` change is not a handoff.

## Builds, tests and frozen subjects

Run builds and tests through `custody.py run` (`<skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py`). It records argv, working directory, environment, wrapper and child PIDs, wait status, output and input digests, and any process still alive afterwards, and prints one line per step. A `--plan` runs a build and its tests in one call: `{"cwd", "env", "env_clear", "steps": [{"name", "argv", "cwd", "env", "env_clear", "digest", "cargo_json", "timeout", "kill_leftovers"}]}`, step values overriding plan values. With `cargo_json` set on a step named `build`, a later step's `{exe:build}` names the test binary it produced (`{exe:build:<target>}` when there are several), and its digest is recorded. Read the one-line results, and open logs only for a failure. Do not write your own runner, or copy PIDs, exit codes or tool-session output into separate records: the record is the custody. In the S10 session of 2026-10-28/29, children referenced 32 helper scripts of their own (13 named `run*`) and 88 tool calls named hand-kept `tool-session.json` records.

To freeze a subject, commit it when it lives in this repository ([slice checkpoint](../../slice-checkpoint/SKILL.md) writes a private ref without moving your branch). For a tree outside it, run `custody.py freeze`: one read of the tree gives a manifest, an archive built from the same bytes, and changes and a diff against a baseline. Task-specific assertions about the frozen subject belong in a check that reads the manifest, not in another freeze script.

<!-- cli-synopsis script=skills/manual-orchestration/scripts/custody.py display="python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py" -->
```text
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py run --out OUT [--name NAME] [--plan PLAN] [--cwd CWD] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--env-clear] [--digest PATH] [--cargo-json] [--timeout SECONDS] [--kill-leftovers] [--keep-going] ...
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py freeze --root ROOT --out OUT [--exclude GLOB] [--baseline-root BASELINE_ROOT] [--baseline-manifest BASELINE_MANIFEST] [--label LABEL]
```
<!-- /cli-synopsis -->

## Result

Return a compact result binding input packet, changed source, binary/schema/fixture where material, test commands and actual outcomes, evidence pointers, failures, unresolved work, invalidated assumptions, process disposition, and your continuation path. Distinguish scripted or private observations from live behavior. Keep requested model and observed runtime identity distinct, and mark unavailable usage or cost unknown.

## Unfinished: handoff

If the assignment remains unfinished, apply `$wind-walker` and write a durable handoff that lets the next owner continue without context-only meaning: objective/authority, exact source/worktree and uncommitted changes, settled decisions and rejected approaches worth keeping, evidence and failed checks, open obligations and pending review, live child/process ownership, and next useful action. Aim for about 500-1,000 tokens plus links without omitting a required obligation. End with `handoff_ready`, the handoff path and SHA-256. This requests transfer; it is neither worker completion nor supervisor acceptance, and it does not release your children or processes. Do not claim a configured campaign's terminal audit receipt from this manual handoff.
# Running on Claude Code (Anthropic models)

The role references are written in Codex terms. On Claude Code the roles,
packets, evidence rules and the retained-or-fresh decision are unchanged; the
mechanics map as below. Load this with your role reference when the session
is Claude Code.

| Codex | Claude Code | difference that matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spawn_agent`, `fork_turns="none"` | `Agent` tool with a non-fork `subagent_type` (`general-purpose`, or a narrower type when it fits) | A `fork` inherits your whole context; it is a retained context, not a fresh one. |
| `followup_task` | `SendMessage` to the agent's ID | **Any** message to a finished agent resumes it with its full transcript. Every `SendMessage` that carries work is a retained dispatch and needs the pre-dispatch check. |
| `wait_agent` | nothing: the harness notifies on completion. The child's result arrives separately, as a framed hand-back message (`SubagentHandback`); the completion notice carries no result text | Do not read or tail a running agent's output file, sleep, or list agents to check progress. Do independent work or end the turn's tool use until notified. |
| requested model and effort | `Agent` `model` (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) | Set `effort` only when the user or an owning instruction asks. Observed model is `message.model` in the transcript. |
| rollout, `session_meta` lineage | `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<root session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and `agent-<id>.meta.json` | The ID is returned by the spawn call. `meta.json` records the description, tool-use ID, `agentType`, `parentAgentId`, `spawnDepth`, `requestShape`, and the requested `model` and `effort`. A nested child's files sit in the **root** session's `subagents/`, with `parentAgentId` naming its parent. The spawn result also names a `tasks/<id>.output` file; it is the full transcript, so do not read it. |
| shared worktree | `Agent` `isolation: "worktree"` | Use it when parallel builders could touch the same files; the worktree is removed if unchanged. **Check the base at entry:** two harness worktrees on 2026-10-22 started at `a69efc44`, 278 commits behind HEAD. The packet names the required base; the worker runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --short`, resets its own clean branch to the base if they differ, records it, and stops if the tree is dirty. |

## Models and review tiers

Model, effort and review-tier choices for this host live in
[model selection](../../../docs/model-selection.md) (the Claude-host rows). Pass the
choice through `Agent` `model` as above. That parameter takes an alias, so record
the observed exact identifier from `message.model`.

## Context check

`<skill-dir>` is the manual-orchestration skill's directory.

```
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/child_context.py \
  claude --transcript <subagents dir>/agent-<id>.jsonl \
  [--next-task-tokens <estimate>] --out <assignment dir>/context-check-N.json
```

The pinned CLI gives the same reading plus accounting:
`<pinned binary> claude --transcript <path> [--json]` for one transcript, and
`<pinned binary> claude-agents --session <id> --with-usage [--json]` for every
subagent of a session (counts each `message.id` once with its maximum output,
and excludes a fork's inherited parent call).

Context is input + cache-creation + cache-read tokens of the latest assistant
call. Transcripts record no window, so the levels are absolute and their basis
differs from Codex:

- **Trigger 150,000** carries over on a cost basis only: every call re-sends
  the whole context, so a retained 160K child pays about six times a fresh
  child's ~25K opening on each call (Codex measurement; the Claude opening is
  `not established`). H1's status is unchanged: a pilot hypothesis.
- **Band floor 202,533** is the lowest of 20 Claude Code auto-compactions on
  this machine as of 2026-10-21 (median 302,526, max 968,704, mixed windows).
  It is a lower bound, not the window.

On 2026-10-21 a coordinator sent a retained re-review to a Claude reviewer
reading 163,367 without running this check, because the skill had no Claude
reader yet. The re-review completed; by H1 it should have been a fresh reviewer
or a recorded overrule (continuity of the reviewer's own findings is a valid
reason).

## Worktree mechanics

- Shells inside an isolated worktree have refused compound commands that mix
  `git` with other programs or `export` variables; run `git` and `cargo` as
  separate plain commands with inline variables (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... cargo ...`).
- A successor launched to continue in an existing worktree is not isolated
  itself: give it the worktree path, and have it use absolute paths,
  `git -C <worktree>` and `--manifest-path`, never the main checkout.
- `SendMessage` to a running agent queues until its next tool round; to a
  finished agent it resumes the full transcript. Use it for bindings and scope
  additions, and count it as a retained dispatch when it carries work.

## Root transfer on Claude Code

The procedure is in [context boundary](context-boundary.md#roots). Claude
specifics:

- The user starts the successor: a new `claude` session in the repository
  directory. The predecessor cannot do it.
- The predecessor's subagents are not reachable from the successor, but their
  transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<old session>/subagents/`) and every
  file they wrote stay readable by path, so handoffs and evidence carry over.
- Hand the user a prompt of this shape, filled in:

```
Act as supervisor under $manual-orchestration (read skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md
and references/supervisor.md by repository path). Continue from the root handoff
<path>, sha256 <digest>, role <role>: verify the digest and run the board's
handoff-status for this role and digest with your own session ID. If superseded,
already adopted, conflicting, or unregistered, reconcile its returned continuation
references and durable authority before adopting or dispatching. Otherwise read
it and the assignment record it names. Use the board's adopt command with your
own session ID, role <role>, predecessor <predecessor-session-id>, and this path
and digest. If adoption succeeds, acknowledge ownership in the assignment record,
re-claim <resources>, post a transition message, then take the next actions it lists.
```

- Bind the successor's identity by reading its own transcript path
  (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<new session id>.jsonl`) and record it.

### Finding and retiring native sessions

Claude Code 2.1.310 supports `--name 'Readable task name | continuation ID'`,
`--resume ID_OR_NAME`, and `agents --json` (`--all` includes completed background
sessions; `--cwd` filters by directory). Use the exact verified ID when resuming;
names need not be unique. A reboot does not make the old assignment current.
The board's published handoff lineage supplies the continuation reference.

`stop ID` stops a background session and retains its conversation. The host
adapter uses this for retirement; interactive sessions are not thereby proven
stopped. `/rename <name>` renames the current conversation and is also documented
for `-p`; use an explicit name to avoid generating one from history. External
renaming of an existing session through the adapter has not been probed.
`rm` can remove a worktree as well as a background-session listing, so it is not
mapped to recoverable archival. These controls were checked with installed
CLI help and the [CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference);
the [commands reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands) covers `/rename`.
they do not establish model identity, task completion, or transfer authority.

## What does not carry over

- The Codex `--session` and `agents` modes read rollouts only; use the `claude`
  and `claude-agents` modes, or `child_context.py claude`, for transcripts.
- The supervisor is the top-level session; subagents are workers or
  reviewers and do not supervise, so their type need not include `Agent`.
- The identity binding is the agent ID and transcript path from the spawn
  result, sent after launch by `SendMessage` as in [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#launching-a-child).
- Repository instructions still apply: Claude subagents read `CLAUDE.md` and
  `AGENTS.md`, and the coordination board is shared with Codex sessions.

## Cost

`metrics/scripts/claude_transcript_usage.py` sums weighted tokens (uncached +
cached/10 + 5 x output, the baseline's unit) for one transcript. Account every
subagent transcript in the task, including the supervisor's own, before a

# Claude Builder

Codex coordinates one coherent engineering assignment; native Claude Code owns
repository understanding, implementation, tests, and repairs within it. Give
Claude the same relevant skills and engineering capabilities available to a Sol
builder. Its model identity changes the execution adapter, not the objective,
acceptance conditions, or access to the existing orchestration machinery.

The caller owns scope, model selection, review selection, result collection,
integration, and final acceptance. Claude's completion report supplies evidence;
it does not authorize publication or accept its own work.

## Assignment and machinery

Use the repository's [manual-orchestration](../manual-orchestration/SKILL.md)
contract: the Codex caller loads its supervisor reference; the
Claude builder loads the worker references and
[Anthropic host mapping](../manual-orchestration/references/anthropic-host.md).
If the packet assigns Claude supervision or decomposition, load that role
instead and provide the needed Agent tools. Tool availability alone does not
assign additional work. Keep the caller responsible for collecting the native
process and any descendants before closing the assignment.

Bind the authoritative repository root and instruction paths in the packet.
Read dependencies from that repository, including when this entrypoint is
installed elsewhere: an older user-scope skill copy must not silently replace
the assigned instructions. Include the accepted outcome, authority, exact
workspace/base and dirty baseline, owned write scope, bounded read set, checks,
settled facts, output/continuation paths, and collection owner. Preserve other
actors' work; a shared workspace is not exclusive ownership.

Keep implementation choices with the builder. Existing repo-search, graph
coverage, deterministic validation, context observation, and Wind Walker
contracts remain applicable. Do not impose the reconnaissance/review skill's
read-only tool profile on this implementation role. Read
[native session controls](references/native-session.md) before launching or
resuming Claude; it explains transport, permissions, identity, and process
collection without introducing another runtime or handoff schema.

## Model choice

Select the model and effort from [model selection](../../docs/model-selection.md):

task or campaign model constraint takes precedence. The builder can recommend a
change, and the caller records the choice and reason in the assignment before
dispatch.

execution evidence. A refusal or substitution fails that turn; the launcher
does not choose a replacement. A provider classifier flag alone establishes
neither that the task is prohibited nor that a successor is prohibited. Assess
the actual requested work under the applicable rules. For otherwise authorized
work, the caller may select a successor under existing user and model guidance.

permission, or transport failures do not establish that a stronger model is

Launch with a predeclared UUID and persistence enabled. Bind that UUID to the
observed result and local transcript. Resume that exact session for subsequent
phases and remediation while its context remains useful. A print-mode process
ending is a turn boundary, not retirement of the builder.

# Worker or reviewer: one coherent assignment

Own the packet's bounded engineering outcome, assigned files and launched processes. At entry, acknowledge the exact packet, authority and source/subject revisions. Your parent sends your identity binding after launch - verified session ID, rollout, parent/collection owner, continuation path, context-status binary and digest; acknowledge it at your next boundary and record it in your continuation. Verify current source and runtime inputs before relying on prior evidence. Read DESIGN.md as AGENTS.md requires; PHILOSOPHY.md in full only for design, planning or doctrine review. Read the coordination board at startup, after compaction and before claims or consequential operations, not as a loop. Before freezing a contract or route revision, check its premises against the packet's settled facts. Select the implementation and checks that establish the actual outcome. Report a discovered requirement gap, stale premise or ownership conflict to the supervisor before expanding scope or silently reclassifying the task. Do not start new child agents or next-slice work unless the packet assigns it.

Follow [call cost](call-cost.md): batch, size requests, do not poll, and message the parent only for a result, a decision, a blocker or a decision-relevant risk.

## Context

When assigned implementer discovery for an organization candidate, use [organization formation](organization-formation.md) to report bounded findings and whether you can own a coherent implementation outcome.

Read only what your packet's read list names; reading spends the same budget as writing. Prefer signatures (`grep -n 'pub fn'`) and targeted line ranges over whole files, batch independent reads, and commit after each independently passing unit.

Keep a compact continuation current as decisions and validation state change, not only when handing off: a compaction takes the window without asking, and the next context holds only what you wrote down. You do not decide the context for your *next* assignment; your parent checks that before dispatching it, because only the parent knows that task's size.

**Mid-task check.** At each logical boundary inside the assignment - before each substantial phase, not once - and again before writing your result if an earlier reading was above about 120,000, run (`<skill-dir>` is the manual-orchestration skill's directory):

```
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/child_context.py \
  --binary <pinned path> --sha256 <digest> check --session <your id> --rollout <your rollout>
```

The script compares your latest input with a trigger of 200,000 tokens and a band floor of 235,000. The floor sits just under the lowest automatic compaction observed: Astra from 239,130, and Sol 6.1 sessions under the 250,000 compaction limit at 248,987 ([measured basis](context-boundary.md#measured-basis)). Both levels are a hypothesis (H2), not a rule. If you are over it and the remaining work is substantial, prepare a handoff; otherwise continue. Record the reading, decision and reason in your continuation. Continuing past the trigger risks a compaction mid-task, after which the rest of the work is done from your continuation alone. If your parent bound a context listener to you, a current observation from it counts as the reading ([session control](context-control.md#what-to-do-with-an-observation)). Use only the binary you were given - do not build to check context, because a build lock can block observation for everyone. If usage cannot be read, record `usage_unavailable` with the script's class; never guess or treat it as zero. An `epoch` change is not a handoff.

## Builds, tests and frozen subjects

Run builds and tests through `custody.py run` (`<skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py`). It records argv, working directory, environment, wrapper and child PIDs, wait status, output and input digests, and any process still alive afterwards, and prints one line per step. A `--plan` runs a build and its tests in one call: `{"cwd", "env", "env_clear", "steps": [{"name", "argv", "cwd", "env", "env_clear", "digest", "cargo_json", "timeout", "kill_leftovers"}]}`, step values overriding plan values. With `cargo_json` set on a step named `build`, a later step's `{exe:build}` names the test binary it produced (`{exe:build:<target>}` when there are several), and its digest is recorded. Read the one-line results, and open logs only for a failure. Do not write your own runner, or copy PIDs, exit codes or tool-session output into separate records: the record is the custody. In the S10 session of 2026-10-28/29, children referenced 32 helper scripts of their own (13 named `run*`) and 88 tool calls named hand-kept `tool-session.json` records.

To freeze a subject, commit it when it lives in this repository ([slice checkpoint](../../slice-checkpoint/SKILL.md) writes a private ref without moving your branch). For a tree outside it, run `custody.py freeze`: one read of the tree gives a manifest, an archive built from the same bytes, and changes and a diff against a baseline. Task-specific assertions about the frozen subject belong in a check that reads the manifest, not in another freeze script.

<!-- cli-synopsis script=skills/manual-orchestration/scripts/custody.py display="python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py" -->
```text
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py run --out OUT [--name NAME] [--plan PLAN] [--cwd CWD] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--env-clear] [--digest PATH] [--cargo-json] [--timeout SECONDS] [--kill-leftovers] [--keep-going] ...
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/custody.py freeze --root ROOT --out OUT [--exclude GLOB] [--baseline-root BASELINE_ROOT] [--baseline-manifest BASELINE_MANIFEST] [--label LABEL]
```
<!-- /cli-synopsis -->

## Result

Return a compact result binding input packet, changed source, binary/schema/fixture where material, test commands and actual outcomes, evidence pointers, failures, unresolved work, invalidated assumptions, process disposition, and your continuation path. Distinguish scripted or private observations from live behavior. Keep requested model and observed runtime identity distinct, and mark unavailable usage or cost unknown.

## Unfinished: handoff

If the assignment remains unfinished, apply `$wind-walker` and write a durable handoff that lets the next owner continue without context-only meaning: objective/authority, exact source/worktree and uncommitted changes, settled decisions and rejected approaches worth keeping, evidence and failed checks, open obligations and pending review, live child/process ownership, and next useful action. Aim for about 500-1,000 tokens plus links without omitting a required obligation. End with `handoff_ready`, the handoff path and SHA-256. This requests transfer; it is neither worker completion nor supervisor acceptance, and it does not release your children or processes. Do not claim a configured campaign's terminal audit receipt from this manual handoff.
# Running on Claude Code (Anthropic models)

The role references are written in Codex terms. On Claude Code the roles,
packets, evidence rules and the retained-or-fresh decision are unchanged; the
mechanics map as below. Load this with your role reference when the session
is Claude Code.

| Codex | Claude Code | difference that matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spawn_agent`, `fork_turns="none"` | `Agent` tool with a non-fork `subagent_type` (`general-purpose`, or a narrower type when it fits) | A `fork` inherits your whole context; it is a retained context, not a fresh one. |
| `followup_task` | `SendMessage` to the agent's ID | **Any** message to a finished agent resumes it with its full transcript. Every `SendMessage` that carries work is a retained dispatch and needs the pre-dispatch check. |
| `wait_agent` | nothing: the harness notifies on completion. The child's result arrives separately, as a framed hand-back message (`SubagentHandback`); the completion notice carries no result text | Do not read or tail a running agent's output file, sleep, or list agents to check progress. Do independent work or end the turn's tool use until notified. |
| requested model and effort | `Agent` `model` (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) | Set `effort` only when the user or an owning instruction asks. Observed model is `message.model` in the transcript. |

The spawn result also names a `tasks/<id>.output` file; it is the full transcript, so do not read it. |
| shared worktree | `Agent` `isolation: "worktree"` | Use it when parallel builders could touch the same files; the worktree is removed if unchanged. **Check the base at entry:** two harness worktrees on 2026-10-22 started at `a69efc44`, 278 commits behind HEAD. The packet names the required base; the worker runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --short`, resets its own clean branch to the base if they differ, records it, and stops if the tree is dirty. |

## Models and review tiers

Model, effort and review-tier choices for this host live in
[model selection](../../../docs/model-selection.md) (the Claude-host rows). Pass the
choice through `Agent` `model` as above. That parameter takes an alias, so record
the observed exact identifier from `message.model`.

## Context check

`<skill-dir>` is the manual-orchestration skill's directory.

```
python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/child_context.py \
  claude --transcript <subagents dir>/agent-<id>.jsonl \
  [--next-task-tokens <estimate>] --out <assignment dir>/context-check-N.json
```

The pinned CLI gives the same reading plus accounting:
`<pinned binary> claude --transcript <path> [--json]` for one transcript, and
`<pinned binary> claude-agents --session <id> --with-usage [--json]` for every
subagent of a session (counts each `message.id` once with its maximum output,
and excludes a fork's inherited parent call).

Context is input + cache-creation + cache-read tokens of the latest assistant
call. Transcripts record no window, so the levels are absolute and their basis
differs from Codex:

- **Trigger 150,000** carries over on a cost basis only: every call re-sends
  the whole context, so a retained 160K child pays about six times a fresh
  child's ~25K opening on each call (Codex measurement; the Claude opening is
  `not established`). H1's status is unchanged: a pilot hypothesis.
- **Band floor 202,533** is the lowest of 20 Claude Code auto-compactions on
  this machine as of 2026-10-21 (median 302,526, max 968,704, mixed windows).
  It is a lower bound, not the window.

On 2026-10-21 a coordinator sent a retained re-review to a Claude reviewer
reading 163,367 without running this check, because the skill had no Claude
reader yet. The re-review completed; by H1 it should have been a fresh reviewer
or a recorded overrule (continuity of the reviewer's own findings is a valid
reason).

## Worktree mechanics

- Shells inside an isolated worktree have refused compound commands that mix
  `git` with other programs or `export` variables; run `git` and `cargo` as
  separate plain commands with inline variables (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... cargo ...`).
- A successor launched to continue in an existing worktree is not isolated
  itself: give it the worktree path, and have it use absolute paths,
  `git -C <worktree>` and `--manifest-path`, never the main checkout.
- `SendMessage` to a running agent queues until its next tool round; to a
  finished agent it resumes the full transcript. Use it for bindings and scope
  additions, and count it as a retained dispatch when it carries work.

## Root transfer on Claude Code

The procedure is in [context boundary](context-boundary.md#roots). Claude
specifics:

- The user starts the successor: a new `claude` session in the repository
  directory. The predecessor cannot do it.
- The predecessor's subagents are not reachable from the successor, but their
  transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<old session>/subagents/`) and every
  file they wrote stay readable by path, so handoffs and evidence carry over.
- Hand the user a prompt of this shape, filled in:

```
Act as supervisor under $manual-orchestration (read skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md
and references/supervisor.md by repository path). Continue from the root handoff
<path>, sha256 <digest>, role <role>: verify the digest and run the board's
handoff-status for this role and digest with your own session ID. If superseded,
already adopted, conflicting, or unregistered, reconcile its returned continuation
references and durable authority before adopting or dispatching. Otherwise read
it and the assignment record it names. Use the board's adopt command with your
own session ID, role <role>, predecessor <predecessor-session-id>, and this path
and digest. If adoption succeeds, acknowledge ownership in the assignment record,
re-claim <resources>, post a transition message, then take the next actions it lists.
```

- Bind the successor's identity by reading its own transcript path
  (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<new session id>.jsonl`) and record it.

### Finding and retiring native sessions

Claude Code 2.1.310 supports `--name 'Readable task name | continuation ID'`,
`--resume ID_OR_NAME`, and `agents --json` (`--all` includes completed background
sessions; `--cwd` filters by directory). Use the exact verified ID when resuming;
names need not be unique. A reboot does not make the old assignment current.
The board's published handoff lineage supplies the continuation reference.

`stop ID` stops a background session and retains its conversation. The host
adapter uses this for retirement; interactive sessions are not thereby proven
stopped. `/rename <name>` renames the current conversation and is also documented
for `-p`; use an explicit name to avoid generating one from history. External
renaming of an existing session through the adapter has not been probed.
`rm` can remove a worktree as well as a background-session listing, so it is not
mapped to recoverable archival. These controls were checked with installed
CLI help and the [CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference);
the [commands reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands) covers `/rename`.
they do not establish model identity, task completion, or transfer authority.

## What does not carry over

- The Codex `--session` and `agents` modes read rollouts only; use the `claude`
  and `claude-agents` modes, or `child_context.py claude`, for transcripts.
- The supervisor is the top-level session; subagents are workers or
  reviewers and do not supervise, so their type need not include `Agent`.
- The identity binding is the agent ID and transcript path from the spawn
  result, sent after launch by `SendMessage` as in [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#launching-a-child).
- Repository instructions still apply: Claude subagents read `CLAUDE.md` and
  `AGENTS.md`, and the coordination board is shared with Codex sessions.

## Cost

`metrics/scripts/claude_transcript_usage.py` sums weighted tokens (uncached +
cached/10 + 5 x output, the baseline's unit) for one transcript. Account every
subagent transcript in the task, including the supervisor's own, before a
total; [measurement](measurement.md) holds the rules.

# Repository Instructions

Before working in this repository, read and follow [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), the

## Pre-release compatibility policy
Work Engine is under active development. Internal implementations and
interfaces have no backward-compatibility guarantee unless an explicit consumer
or owner-approved contract requires one.  Prefer the simplest architecture that
satisfies current requirements and the intended system design.  Existing code
is reusable implementation material, not architectural authority. It may be
modified, replaced, or removed.  Preserve approved semantics, data integrity,
provenance, and qualification evidence—not obsolete implementation behavior.
Any recommendation to preserve compatibility must identify the specific
consumer, the consequence of breaking it, and the cost of maintaining it.  

## Model-selection guidance
[Model selection](docs/model-selection.md) provides current defaults and their
tradeoffs when choosing an engineering model. It is decision guidance, not an
override of explicit user choices or campaign/provider contracts; consult it
when that choice is in scope, rather than inferring a selection from inheritance.

## Rust development direction

[Rust development](docs/rust-development.md) records the user's Rust-first
direction for new first-party implementation and proposed shared-code boundaries.
Use it when choosing implementation language or reusable package placement;
existing components and their authority remain until accepted replacement.

## Where files go

Readers judge a file's standing from where it sits. Put a new file where
[repository layout](docs/repository-layout.md) says, and follow its rules when
moving or citing one.

## Coordinating sub-agents

Outside a configured Slice Builder campaign, a Codex or Claude Code session
that coordinates sub-agents, or that a parent launches under
[the manual-orchestration skill](skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md), uses
that skill and loads only the references it names for the active role. A
child launched under another skill or review contract follows that contract.

## Durable role schedules

Scheduled obligations can outlive model context, but a schedule does not create
authority or activate an agent. When a durable scheduler capability is
configured and this session has an active human-supervised role, read and
follow [the role-scheduler skill](skills/role-scheduler/SKILL.md) at startup.
Reconcile overdue, due, and near-term items before ordinary work that could make
them stale or invisible. Do not emulate durable scheduling by storing future
obligations only in model context or an unobserved terminal.

In the first turn of every new context window created by a session restart,
context reset, or compaction, invoke and follow `$wind-walker` before resuming
unfinished work. Perform this invocation in the new context window so the
skill governs recovery and continuation there.

continuation-critical objectives, authority boundaries, commitments,
unresolved obligations, and references have durable owners. If that cannot be
established, do not replace context.

the new context window and stop rather than continue when correct recovery
still depends on meaning lost with the prior context.

repository chatboard:

```bash
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . read --limit 20 --active-claims
```

campaign references. Use `claim` before operating on a shared campaign,
ordinal, reviewer episode, or publication resource, and `release` when done.
